Our very own Nick O’Neill is has launched a new stream covering crypto, finance, AI, tech, and the stories shaping the internet economy.

If you already follow Nick, you know what to expect: sharp takes, market chaos, founder brain, and the occasional banger you’ll see clipped on the timeline five minutes later.

Episodes will be streaming live on YouTube, so make sure you’re subscribed to catch the next one as it happens.

**[Subscribe to Choose Rich Live!](https://www.youtube.com/@chooserichnick/streams)**

———————————————————————————

## Top Stories

**BTC** $64,364 (1.7%) | **ETH** $1,910 (1.8%) | **SOL** $74 (0.8%)

* Claude Mythos [cracks post-quantum](https://decrypt.co/374600/claude-mythos-cracked-post-quantum-cryptography) signature scheme

* South Korean finance minister to hold [emergency meeting](https://x.com/solidintel_x/status/2082383791264305285?s=20) after KOSPI volatility

* Fed hike odds [hit 30%](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2082154863815786521) before decision today

* Apple [overtakes Nvidia](https://decrypt.co/374604/apple-overtakes-nvidia-which-bigger-july) as the world's most valuable company and becomes the second company ever to hit [$5T market cap](https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2082099016163058153)

* Zcash activates ["Ironwood"](https://x.com/DegenerateNews/status/2082111170626851180), launching a formally verified new shielded pool with turnstile supply checks

* Morgan Stanley launches[ Solana ETP](https://x.com/tokens/status/2082425913384521948?s=20)

* SK Hynix perp contract on Hyperliquid [flips BTC](https://x.com/DegenerateNews/status/2082384852628685184?s=20) in 24h volume

* Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev adds new X safeguards to block social engineering after [support handed over his account](https://x.com/DegenerateNews/status/2082127606275576233)

Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our editor-in-chief. A boyfriend I had at university in Tokyo once told me that older teammates from his sports club had taken him to a sex parlour. So I was not surprised to learn that 48% of Japanese men have paid for sex at some point, compared with 11% of British men. In Japan the industry is woven into male social life—but it has rarely been the subject of serious debate, and the laws governing it are murky. This year, though, sex work became a political issue. The trigger was a rise in street prostitution around a park in Tokyo. It stands out in a country where most of the trade happens behind closed doors. Nor has it helped that many of the men approaching these women are foreign tourists taking advantage of a weak yen. For some Japanese men—even those who think nothing of buying sex themselves—that stings their pride. In the booming 1970s and 80s, it was Japanese men who flew abroad for it. **Welcome back!** Claude found weaknesses in encryption that human experts missed for years, and 1,132 of the people building frontier AI asked Washington to slow their own employers down. Meanwhile Trump closed the border to Chinese robots and Microsoft unveiled an AI that plays attacker and defender at the same time.



**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** Is Mythos really that good?

* **The letter:** Why did OpenAI and Anthropic employees ask the USA to slow their companies down?

* **Trump:** Which Chinese machines just got banned?

* **Microsoft:** Why does its new AI attack the people it protects?


----------



----------
## [Mythos poked holes in unbreakable encryption](https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7fc42b99-f810-44a8-aaa3-a508eda6bfb3/Beehiiv_01_-_Jul_29.png?t=1785319132)
Caption: 

Encryption is the math keeping your bank login and your messages private, and it holds for one reason. The world's best mathematicians attack it for years and come up empty.

Anthropic pointed Claude Mythos at two of its most studied pieces, and Mythos found gaps in both.

HAWK is a signature scheme built to survive quantum computers. Human experts reviewed it for two years and passed it twice, and Mythos cut its strength in half in 60 hours.

It also made the best-known attack on a weakened version of AES, the cipher behind most internet traffic, 200 to 800 times faster.

Claude turned the AES job down at first, insisting there was nothing left to find. Three days of pep talks and a billion tokens later, it had the attack.

Plenty of ciphers guarding real systems have had far less review than these two, and Anthropic's own researchers needed a month to verify a week of Claude's work.

Nothing you use today breaks. Both were research targets.
